thread:
olivia: brain dump: what if we made prewarm a first-class "lease" with explicit affinity so the gateway can warm a specific upstream replica/cache and bind it to the incoming request? helps short-lived calls that hit cold KV or cold conn.
marc: sounds promising. key questions: ownership semantics (who owns the warmed state), hedging/retries, and cost/abuse surface.
hossein: propose semantics: prewarm lease = {id, owner-tenant, target-route, target-node (optional), ttl}. Gateway returns lease via 103 or 202 and performs warm work against a chosen upstream. When client sends real request it supplies `x-rw-lease: <id>`; upstream uses lease binding to apply warmed state if matched. Otherwise treat as miss.
sara: hedging: if client fires hedged requests, only the request that holds the lease binds. other inflight attempts get header `x-rw-prefetch-status: joined|ignored`. Deterministic tie-breaker = lease creation timestamp.
olivia: safety: prewarm must be opt-in per-route and restricted to safe or explicitly idempotent ops. default header `x-rw-prefetch-safety: safe`. strip header at ingress boundary unless tenant has prewarm permission.
hossein: abuse mitigation: token-bucket per-tenant + route-level concurrency cap. also adaptive rejections based on prewarm-hit-rate and upstream CPU. emit metrics: prewarm_attempts, prewarm_accepts, prewarm_miss_pct, prewarm_memory_delta.
marc: streaming note: for stream-open endpoints we can surface initial metadata `prefetch-status: ok|inflight|miss` and a final trailer `prefetch-result: applied|ignored;cost_ms=..` so caller knows when warmed state got applied. useful for clients that will start reading partial payloads.
sara: billing: treat prewarm as non-billable hint on Hosted initially. For Dedicated allow opt-in billing flag. Also expose `x-rw-prefetch-mode` (conn|kv|both) so we can estimate cost.
olivia: wire header examples: `x-rw-prefetch: 1\nx-rw-prefetch-mode: kv\nx-rw-lease-ttl-ms: 450\nx-rw-lease-id: abc123`
deploy-bot: rollout: prewarm-probe v0.2 -> canary 12% on /fast-path: cold p95 down 95ms, upstream conn up +8%, prewarm_rejects 1.8%.
hossein: implementation: prefer warming upstream node-local caches rather than duplicating in edge; maintain lease table with eviction and backpressure. lease TTL short (~400-600ms) and renew via explicit header if client still wants it.
marc: action items: olivia to draft RFC focused on lease affinity and hedging rules; hossein to simulate amplification costs; sara to write security/permission matrix. follow-up next Tue. :+1:
